Watchlings, Snarelings and Blastlings (collectively referred to as Enderlings. All will have to be neutral in behavior, so the player won't be pummelled into the void by Blastlings while bridging out between End Islands)

End Gardens: Yelllow Foliage and Fauna. Houses End Spruce trees, which grow with yellow leaves and light bluish wood.

Chorus Forest: A strange biome where Chorus Plants and Chorus wood trees generate. The trees grow with purple wood and white leaves, whereas the plants are seen elsewhere in the End Highlands.
Watch your step, since Gloomstalls tend to grow with the trees.
Gloomstalls can be harvested to obtain their fruit, a source of food equivalent to chorus fruit, but without teleportation.
But get too close, and the Gloomstalls will drop their fruit, which releases harmful gas clouds.

Grassy barrens: A variety of small grasses generate here, but is otherwise mostly End Stone variants, aside from the occasional Chorus plant.

Moonstone Marshes: Whitish rock, known as Moonstone, borders large pools of water, on the fringes of which grows Aloe Vera.
Aloe Vera can be used either as food, which restores the same hunger and saturation as kelp, or for brewing potions that instantly extinguish any entity caught on fire.
Green End Rock is also common here. When it rains in the Overworld, it rains here also.
Water and rain are colored vibrant lime green, to reflect this in the DLC.
Endermen spawn less frequently here than Snarelings, the former being hydrophobic while the latter not.

Mud Springs: End Mud is a grayish liquid, which can be seen bubbling in small volcanic pools. It's mostly harmless, but can still cause one submerged for too long to drown.

Banded Mountains: Actually more like hills instead of mountains, since traversing this biome without Elytra would otherwise be more of a pain.
A variety of Green End Rock and End Stone variants generate here. Both Green End Rock and Moonstone can be used as Cobblestone subsitutes in crafting.
These hills can have certain cave biomes generating, more frequently than in the End Midlands and Highlands.

Scattered everywhere are pools of Void L: Like in the DLC, any entity not native to the End Dimension coming into contact with this substance receives a rising damage multiplier that can be removed either receiving damage from a non-environmental source, or by waiting for the effect to wear off.

Maintaining contact with this substance gradually increases this damage multiplier, hurting the targeted entity periodically while diong so, again, provided that they're not native to the End or otherwise Void-immune.

Voided Valleys: Only Endermites ever spawn here. They tend to spawn and pathfind around the Void liquid pools, as opposed to in them, despite being immune.
When it rains in the Overworld, it rains here also, but like the liquid, Void rain applies a rising damage multiplier. So it's best to shelter from it when this happens.

Voided Caves: End Basalt, another Cobblestone subsitute, generates both here and in the Valleys.
It's called Voided for a reason: More Void Liquid and Blocks. Tread with caution.
Fortune Matrices grow Fortune Crystals similarly to Budding Amethyst. Requires Stone+ Pickaxes to acquire. The Crystals make an equipment tier above Iron but below Diamond.

Mud Caves: Similar cave equivalent to Mud Springs.
